chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from whoever mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Zamzam used to be whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and it flowed freely. Then it transgressed against the other waters, so God — Majestic and Mighty — resented it and caused a spring of aloe to flow over it.

key_terms.أَغَارَهَا: caused it to be changed/adulterated — possibly from غار meaning to become jealous/resentful, or from the causative form meaning to mix and diminish quality
key_terms.الْأَمْيَاهِ: waters — plural of ماء (water), referring to other natural water sources
key_terms.بَغَتْ: transgressed/acted arrogantly — from بَغَى, meaning to exceed proper bounds, act unjustly, or boast
key_terms.جَلَّ وَعَزَّ: Majestic and Mighty — divine epithet, same as جل جلاله (may His majesty be glorified)
key_terms.زَمْزَمُ: Zamzam — the sacred well in the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, believed to have been miraculously created for Hajar (Hagar) and Ishmael
key_terms.سَائِحَةً: flowing freely — from the root س-ي-ح, meaning to flow unrestrained or to wander
key_terms.صَبِرٍ: aloe (Aloe vera) — the bitter plant whose juice, when mixed with water, makes it bitter and medicinal

ai.seo_question: Why did Zamzam water become bitter according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a cosmological tradition about the sacred Zamzam well in Mecca, attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS). The water of Zamzam is described as having originally been of extraordinary purity and sweetness — whiter than milk and sweeter than honey — but that it overflowed and became prideful over other waters. As divine punishment for this arrogance, God caused a bitter spring of aloe to flow into it, altering its character permanently. This narrative anthropomorphizes the sacred spring and conveys the theological lesson that pride and transgression — even in natural phenomena — invite divine correction.
word_analysis: so He caused it to be mixed/adulterated

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

Zazam used to be more intensely whiter than the milk, and sweeter than the honey, and it burst its banks and it boasted about it, so it was came upon by the (other) waters. So Allahazwj Majestic and Mighty Resented it and Caused a spring of aloe to flow over it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the water of Zamzam was whiter than milk, sweeter than honey and it flowed. It then oppressed other waters. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, made it to sink and a fountain of Saber e (aloe) to flow on it.’”
